# How to use this document

This is the full, agreed plan for adding job tracking to hpcR. It is written so
that an implementing agent can work from it without the original conversation,
and so that a human can audit the decisions and examples.

* **Status:** design is settled. No code has been written. Items in
  [Open items to verify](#open-items) are things the implementer must check in
  the code before relying on them (they could not be confirmed during design).
* **Read order for an implementer:** Sections 1-4 (scope, background,
  terminology, decisions), then 5-12 (the design), then 14-16 (file-by-file
  changes, tests, build order). Section 13 (phase 2) is **not** to be built now.
* **Conventions to follow:** the package uses S7, `cli` for messages
  (`cli::cli_abort()` etc.), `+` builders in `R/sugar.R`, roxygen docs with
  `@noRd` for internal functions, and testthat 3e. Keep new code consistent
  with the surrounding files.
* **Do not** commit this file; the `local/` folder is git-ignored and
  `.Rbuildignore`d.

# Goal and scope

## Goal

Let users opt in to recording what happens to submitted jobs (and sequences of
jobs) in a database, and query that record with one friendly function,
`status()`. The machinery comes from BrainGnomes
(`R/job_tracking_functions.R`, `R/job_reconciliation.R`,
`R/sqlite_functions.R`, and the `inst/` CLI scripts), re-designed for hpcR.

## In scope (phase 1: build now)

1. Uppercase status vocabulary across the whole package.
2. `submit()` returns the job/sequence with submission data; new `job_id()`.
3. Opt-in `+ track()` with a SQLite backend behind S7 generics.
4. Sequence support (every job in a sequence shares one DB; dependency edges
   recorded with their `wait_signal`).
5. Compute-side status updates (`RUNNING`, `COMPLETED`, `FAILED`) from the
   scheduler templates, with robust fallbacks.
6. `status()` (works with or without tracking) and `class_job_status`.
7. Reconciliation of the DB against the scheduler and the fallback log.
8. User-supplied tags set at submit time.
9. `inst/` reorganization into subfolders.

## Out of scope for now (deferred)

* **Job contracts** (immutable manifests, runtime receipts, submission-attempt
  registry). These are a provenance layer on top of tracking, with
  BrainGnomes-specific fields (`stage`, `stream`, `sub_id`, `ses_id`).
* **Output manifests** (`capture_output_manifest()` in BrainGnomes).
* **Projects** (grouping DBs). The DB-naming code is isolated in one function so
  this can be added later.
* **Storing a serialized job object (`job_obj` BLOB)** per row.
* **Phase 2** (Section 13): sub-jobs spawned from inside a running job, and
  runtime tags set from inside a script.

# Background: what exists today

## hpcR (verified in this worktree)

* `R/job_methods.R`: `submit(class_job)` currently returns `invisible(<scheduler
  id>)`. It calls `.hydrate_defaults`, `.validate_job`, `.prepare_job_packages`,
  `.compile_job`, then `.submit_job`. `submit(class_job_sequence)` loops over
  ready nodes, calls `submit(job)`, keeps `submitted_ids` (named by object ID)
  and passes `scheduler@sequencing@upstream_ids`; it returns
  `invisible(submitted_ids)`. `clone()` is implemented (`.clone_object()` gives a
  new `object_id` and `created_at`); only its NEWS entry is stale.
* `R/check_job_status.R`: `.standardize_statuses()` maps scheduler states to the
  lowercase set `queued, running, suspended, complete, failed, cancelled,
  missing, unknown`. Backends: `.check_job_status_slurm()` (`sacct -X -P`; a
  non-zero exit warns and returns `missing` for all jobs),
  `.check_job_status_torque()` (`qstat -f`, then `tracejob`, one call per job;
  cancel detection is a text regex; exit status 0 means complete),
  `.check_job_status_local()` (`ps`; a PID absent from `ps` is assumed
  complete, so a killed local job looks complete; local is unsupported on
  Windows via `.assert_local_supported`).
* `R/wait_for_job.R`: uses `terminal_statuses <- c("failed","cancelled",
  "complete")` and `.give_status_update()`; already documents the idea of a
  parent script waiting on the sub-jobs it spawns.
* `R/utils.R`: `.job_obj_guard(x, fn, alt_fn = NULL)` aborts when handed a job
  object (used by `check_job_status()` and `wait_for_job()`); it supports an
  `alt_fn` hint line.
* `R/update_job.R`: `+` is defined only for `(class_job, class_job_update)`,
  with `overwrite`/`warn_overwrite`; lines ~103-105 already warn about
  overwritten properties. `class_job_sequence` is defined in `R/job_classes.R`
  (~line 336).
* `R/submit_job.R`: dependency setting is `wait_signal` with options `afterok`
  (default), `after`, `afterany`, `afterburstbuffer`, `aftercorr`,
  `afternotok`.
* `R/compile_job.R`: `.get_system_file()` is the **only** place that resolves
  `inst/` file paths (`submit_to_slurm.sbatch`, `submit_to_torque.pbs`,
  `submit_to_local.sh`, `run_r_job.R`) via `system.file()`.
* `R/defaults.R`: `.hydrate_defaults` / `.job_defaults()` hold package defaults.
* `inst/run_r_job.R` is a standalone wrapper (parses args, loads packages,
  `source()`s the user script inside `tryCatch`). It contains `TODO` comments
  marking where status updates belong (STARTED, FAILED+cascade, COMPLETED) and
  commented-out sub-job code (`wait_for_subs`, `SUB_JOB_IDS`).
* NEWS: compute-time runners were deliberately made light (no `pacman`,
  `R.utils`, `cli`).
* Tests that will need updating: `tests/testthat/test-status-wait.R`,
  `test-run.R` (~lines 95, 202), `test-submit-invoke.R` (~lines 172, 177, 256,
  347, 445). `test-submit-invoke.R` line ~177 already anticipates
  `submit(sequence)` returning an updated sequence. About 73 lowercase status
  strings appear across `R/`, tests, vignettes and README.

## BrainGnomes (reference; `zacharyvig/BrainGnomes`)

* Statuses: `QUEUED, STARTED, FAILED, COMPLETED, FAILED_BY_EXT, CANCELLED`.
  `FAILED_BY_EXT` means "a downstream job's upstream failed and the sequence is
  set to stop on failure".
* `child_level` (1 = downstream, 2 = sub-job) is only a label written by
  `add_tracked_job_parent()`. The cascade is a recursive query over
  `parent_id`; levels are **not** needed once an edge table exists.
* `inst/upd_job_status.R`: retries resolving the job row up to 40 times (0.25 s
  apart) for `STARTED` (short-job race); writes are strict when a DB is given.
* SQLite practices worth keeping: `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, a 10 s busy handler,
  compare-and-set updates, schema migrations by `ALTER TABLE`.
* `reconcile_tracked_jobs()`: selects non-terminal rows (and externally failed
  rows without scheduler confirmation), queries the scheduler in chunks of 200
  per scheduler, plans actions (`UPDATE_TERMINAL_FAILURE`, `VERIFY_OUTPUTS`,
  `CONFIRM_OUTCOME`), `dry_run = TRUE` by default, stops early if the scheduler
  is unavailable.
* CLI scripts in `inst/` (`insert_tracked_job.R`, `upd_job_status.R`,
  `add_parent.R`) are thin wrappers that parse `--flags` and call package
  functions; templates call them with traps for `SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP/SIGQUIT`.
  The sibling package `fmri.pipeline` does the same, and its `R_batch_job`
  class writes status calls directly into a generated R wrapper.

# Terminology (strict)

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **upstream / downstream** | Jobs related by a sequence (`a %->% b`: `a` is upstream of `b`). |
| **parent / child (sub-job)** | A job that itself spawns jobs while running. **Never** use for `%->%`. Phase 2 only. |
| **sequence** | A `class_job_sequence` (jobs plus dependency edges). |
| **row** | One tracked submission in the DB (`row_id`). |
| **breadcrumb** | A line in the hpcR fallback log written when a compute-side hook cannot reach the DB (Section 10.5). |
| **reported by** | Who established a row's status: `JOB`, `SCHEDULER`, or `INFERRED`. |
| **reconciliation** | Comparing DB rows (and breadcrumbs) against the scheduler and repairing them. |

No `parent_id` or `child_level` columns for sequences. A reserved nullable
`parent_row` column exists for phase 2 sub-jobs.

# Decision log

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| 1 | Tracking is **opt-in** via `+ track()`. |
| 2 | Job contracts are deferred. |
| 3 | `status()` is the main query function; `check_job_status()` stays the advanced scheduler-level function. |
| 4 | Default tracking timeout is 10 s; set globally with `options(hpcR.tracking_timeout = )` or per job with `track(timeout = )`. |
| 5 | `track()` takes only an optional `db` path (SQLite file, created if missing). Folder choice goes through `job_directory()`. |
| 6 | Default DB: `<job_directory>/.hpcR/hpcR_<basename>.sqlite`; file name computed in one internal function (`.tracking_db_name()`). |
| 7 | All jobs in a sequence share one DB. Explicit differing `db` paths in one sequence are an error; derived locations never conflict. |
| 8 | `a %->% b + track()` parses as `(a %->% b) + track()`; a new `+` method applies it to every member job. |
| 9 | One uppercase status vocabulary package-wide (package is unreleased): `QUEUED RUNNING SUSPENDED COMPLETED FAILED CANCELLED SKIPPED MISSING UNKNOWN` plus `UNAVAILABLE`. |
| 10 | `SKIPPED` replaces `FAILED_BY_EXT`. `QUEUED` is kept (not `PENDING`). |
| 11 | `submit()` returns the job/sequence carrying submission data; `job_id()` is the accessor; a print method shows the ID so an unassigned result is not lost. No hint on unassigned results. |
| 12 | `check_job_status()`/`wait_for_job()` keep rejecting job objects, with an added hint to use `job_id()`. |
| 13 | `status()` works with or without tracking (resolution by input type, Section 9). |
| 14 | Dependency graph stored as an edge table with the `wait_signal` per edge; no levels. |
| 15 | Backend abstraction: S7 generics (`tracking_*`) dispatching on `class_tracking_backend`; SQLite is the first (only) implementation. |
| 16 | The cascade is `tracking_cascade()`; an `include_children` argument arrives with phase 2. |
| 17 | Reconciliation is in phase 1. `status(refresh = FALSE)` is the default; a staleness hint is printed. |
| 18 | Tags (user key/value info supplied at submit time) are in phase 1. |
| 19 | The scheduler templates (all languages) own the `RUNNING/COMPLETED/FAILED` writes. `run_r_job.R` holds only R-only logic (sub-jobs, phase 2). |
| 20 | hpcR must be installed on compute nodes for tracked jobs, but hook failures must never affect the job (robust fallbacks, Section 10). |
| 21 | Fallback log ("breadcrumb") is hpcR-specific, read by reconciliation; scheduler/job logs are never parsed. |
| 22 | Put code in existing files; only one new R file, `R/tracking.R`. |
| 23 | `inst/` is reorganized into subfolders. |

# User-facing API

## Building and submitting

```{r}
job <- rjob("preproc") + script("preproc.R") + scheduler("slurm") +
  resources(cpus = 4, memory = "8G") +
  track()                                   # default DB under job_directory()

job <- submit(job)        # returns the job WITH submission data (assign it!)
job_id(job)               # scheduler id, e.g. "4821"
status(job)               # reads the tracking DB

track("path/to/my.sqlite")                   # explicit DB
track(timeout = 30)                          # per-job timeout (seconds)
track(tags = list(subject = "01", step = "preproc"))

# sequence: tracking applies to every member job
sq <- (a %->% b %->% c) + track()
sq <- submit(sq)
job_id(sq)                # named vector: names = object ids
status(sq)                # upstream -> downstream tree
```

If the user forgets to assign, the visible return value prints:

```
<hpcR job "preproc"> submitted
  scheduler: slurm   job id: 4821   tracking: ./.hpcR/hpcR_preproc.sqlite
```

## Function reference

| Function | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `track(db = NULL, timeout = NULL, cascade = TRUE, tags = NULL)` | `R/sugar.R` | Builds a `class_job_update` that sets the `.tracking` property (a `class_pb_tracking`). |
| `status(x, ..., refresh = FALSE)` | `R/job_methods.R` | S7 generic; see Section 9. Returns `class_job_status`. |
| `job_id(x)` | `R/job_methods.R` | Scalar for a job, named character vector for a sequence, `character(0)` if unsubmitted. |
| `tracking_*` generics | `R/tracking.R` | Exported as advanced/developer-facing (Section 7.3). |
| `check_job_status()`, `wait_for_job()` | existing | Uppercase statuses; reject job objects with a `job_id()` hint. |

# Status vocabulary

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `QUEUED` | Submitted, not started. |
| `RUNNING` | Started on a node. |
| `SUSPENDED` | Scheduler-suspended. |
| `COMPLETED` | Finished successfully. |
| `FAILED` | Finished unsuccessfully (non-zero exit, timeout, OOM, node failure...). |
| `CANCELLED` | Cancelled by user/scheduler. |
| `SKIPPED` | **Will not run** because an upstream job's outcome made its dependency unsatisfiable and the sequence is set to stop (replaces BrainGnomes `FAILED_BY_EXT`). Never started. |
| `MISSING` | Scheduler no longer knows the job and there is no other evidence. |
| `UNKNOWN` | A scheduler state hpcR cannot map. |
| `UNAVAILABLE` | The scheduler query itself failed (distinct from `MISSING`). Query-time value; not stored as a row status. |

Terminal statuses: `COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED, SKIPPED`.
Non-terminal ("pending"): `QUEUED, RUNNING, SUSPENDED`.

**Migration:** change case in `.standardize_statuses()` (keep the existing
state mapping, rename `complete` to `COMPLETED`), `wait_for_job()`'s
`terminal_statuses`, print/summary code, docs, vignettes, README, and tests.
Grep for lowercase literals (about 73). Add `UNAVAILABLE` to the Slurm path
when `sacct` exits non-zero (today it returns `missing` for every job, which
conflates "scheduler unreachable" with "job not found").

## `reported_by`

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `JOB` | The job's own hook (or its breadcrumb) reported it. |
| `SCHEDULER` | Reconciliation obtained it from `sacct`/`qstat`/`ps`. |
| `INFERRED` | Derived by the cascade (e.g. `SKIPPED`), not observed. |

# Data model

## DB location

* `track(db = NULL)`: `db` is an optional path to a SQLite file; created if
  missing (parent dirs created).
* Default: `<job_directory>/.hpcR/hpcR_<basename>.sqlite`, computed only by
  `.tracking_db_name()` / `.resolve_tracking_db()`. Resubmitting the same job
  reuses the same file because directory and name are stable.
* Sequences: if members carry different **explicit** `db` paths, abort naming
  them. Derived (default) locations never conflict: use the first tracked
  job's job directory and emit one message naming the DB.
* Open item: confirm exactly what `<basename>` is (planned: the job's
  `job_name`; for a sequence, the first/root tracked job's name).

## Schema (SQLite, `PRAGMA user_version = 1`)

```{sql}
CREATE TABLE job_tracking (
  row_id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  object_id       TEXT NOT NULL,          -- hpcR job object_id
  sequence_id     TEXT,                   -- shared by all jobs of one sequence
  job_name        TEXT,
  scheduler_name  TEXT NOT NULL,          -- slurm | torque | local
  scheduler_job_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  status          TEXT NOT NULL,
  reported_by     TEXT NOT NULL,          -- JOB | SCHEDULER | INFERRED
  parent_row      INTEGER,                -- RESERVED for phase 2 sub-jobs (NULL now)
  submit_time     TEXT,
  start_time      TEXT,
  end_time        TEXT,
  exit_code       INTEGER,
  note            TEXT,                   -- e.g. 'recovered from breadcrumb: hpcR_not_found'
  job_directory   TEXT,
  breadcrumb      TEXT,                   -- path of the fallback log for this row
  created_at      TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at      TEXT NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (scheduler_name, scheduler_job_id)
);

CREATE TABLE job_dependencies (
  upstream_row    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES job_tracking(row_id),
  downstream_row  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES job_tracking(row_id),
  signal          TEXT NOT NULL,          -- the edge's wait_signal
  PRIMARY KEY (upstream_row, downstream_row)
);

CREATE TABLE job_tags (
  row_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES job_tracking(row_id),
  key     TEXT NOT NULL,
  value   TEXT,
  source  TEXT NOT NULL,                  -- SUBMIT now; RUNTIME in phase 2
  set_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (row_id, key)
);

CREATE TABLE tracking_events (            -- applied breadcrumb lines (idempotency)
  event_key  TEXT PRIMARY KEY,            -- "<job_id>|<status>|<timestamp>"
  row_id     INTEGER,
  applied_at TEXT NOT NULL
);
```

Connection practice: `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` for writes, busy timeout = the job's
tracking timeout (default 10 s). Writers must **refuse to write** if
`user_version` is greater than the installed hpcR understands.
Timestamps: ISO-8601 UTC text.

## S7 classes (in `R/job_classes.R`)

| Class | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `class_pb_tracking` | Property block stored in the job's `.tracking` property: `db` (chr or NULL), `backend` (`"sqlite"`), `timeout` (num or NULL), `cascade` (lgl, default `TRUE`), `tags` (named list). |
| `class_tracking_backend` | Abstract; dispatch target for the generics. |
| `class_tracking_sqlite` | Subclass holding `db` path and `timeout`. **Built at use time from the job's `class_pb_tracking`; never stored in the job.** |
| `class_job_status` | A tibble plus `source` (`"tracking"` or `"scheduler"`), `db` path, `queried_at`. Has print, `as.data.frame`, `as_tibble` methods. |

No `class_tracked_job`; rows are tibbles. Jobs gain properties `.tracking`
(`class_pb_tracking` or NULL) and `.submission` (list: scheduler job id,
scheduler name, submit time, db path; NULL until submitted). Properties
starting with `.` are already excluded from scheduler directives by
`.get_scheduler_arguments(exclude = "^[.]")`; keep it that way.

## Generics (in `R/tracking.R`)

All dispatch on `backend` (a `class_tracking_backend`); the SQLite methods live
in the same file.

| Generic | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `tracking_init(backend)` | Create/migrate schema; set `user_version`. |
| `tracking_register(backend, jobs, edges, tags)` | Insert rows (status `QUEUED`, `reported_by = "JOB"` since the submitter is recording its own submission), edges and tags; return `row_id`s. |
| `tracking_update(backend, row_id, status, reported_by, expected_status = NULL, exit_code = NULL, end_time = NULL, note = NULL, cascade = FALSE)` | Compare-and-set update (`WHERE status = expected_status` when given); returns logical (updated or not). Cascade per Section 8.3. |
| `tracking_resolve_id(backend, scheduler_job_id, scheduler_name = NULL, retries = 0, wait = 0.25)` | Scheduler id to `row_id`, with retry for the short-job race. |
| `tracking_query(backend, row_id = NULL, sequence_id = NULL, object_id = NULL)` | Return rows (and edges/tags) as tibbles. |
| `tracking_pending(backend)` | Rows whose status is non-terminal, or `reported_by = INFERRED`. |
| `tracking_cascade(backend, row_id)` | Propagate a terminal outcome to downstream rows by edge `signal`. (`include_children` added in phase 2.) |
| `tracking_reconcile(backend, dry_run = TRUE, ...)` | Section 11. Returns an action tibble. |

# Submission, `job_id()` and the guard

* `submit(class_job)` returns the job (visibly) with `.submission` filled in.
  `submit(class_job_sequence)` returns the sequence with each member updated.
  Update the existing assertions/tests that capture the old return value.
* If the job has `.tracking`: resolve the DB, `tracking_init()`, build the
  `class_tracking_sqlite` backend, `tracking_register()` after the scheduler id
  is known, and record edges with the edge `wait_signal`.
* `job_id(x)`: scalar for a job; named character vector (names = object ids) for
  a sequence; `character(0)` if unsubmitted.
* `.job_obj_guard()`: keep aborting on job objects, and add a line:
  "Use `job_id(job)` to get the scheduler id."
* Print methods (in `R/print_job.R`) show scheduler, job id, tracking DB.

# Sequences

## 8.1 Applying `track()`

Add `+` for `(class_job_sequence, class_job_update)` in `R/update_job.R`: apply
the update to every member job, reusing the existing overwrite logic. The
overwrite warning (already present for single jobs) must **name the jobs**.

## 8.2 Partial tracking

Only tracked jobs are recorded. At submit, emit one message listing untracked
members and suggesting `+ track()` on the whole sequence. A tracked job whose
upstream job is untracked gets a warning (its dependency cannot be recorded).

## 8.3 Edges and the cascade

Edges are recorded in `job_dependencies` with the edge's `wait_signal`.

When a job reaches a terminal state (via a hook or reconciliation) and
`cascade = TRUE`, walk downstream edges recursively (recursive CTE):

| Edge `signal` | Upstream outcome that makes the downstream job unsatisfiable |
|---|---|
| `afterok`, `aftercorr` | upstream `FAILED` or `CANCELLED` |
| `afternotok` | upstream `COMPLETED` |
| `afterany`, `after`, `afterburstbuffer` | never (no cascade) |

Affected downstream rows that are still `QUEUED` become `SKIPPED` with
`reported_by = INFERRED` and a `note` naming the upstream job. Rows already
terminal or `RUNNING` are left alone. Local jobs: treat edges as `afterok`
unless the edge says otherwise (open item: local dependencies appear to be
polling-based via `repolling_interval`/`max_wait`; verify).

**Unsatisfiable dependency, explained.** With `afterok`, if the upstream job
fails the downstream job can never start. Slurm leaves it `PENDING` with reason
`DependencyNeverSatisfied` unless `kill_invalid_depend` is set; Torque holds it
similarly. Without intervention it sits in the queue forever. The cascade marks
it `SKIPPED` so the database reflects reality, and reconciliation later notes
whether it should be cancelled in the scheduler (Section 11).

# `status()`

## 9.1 Resolution by input type

| Input | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Tracked job or sequence (submitted) | Read the DB (`source = "tracking"`). |
| Path to a SQLite tracking file | Read that DB. |
| Scheduler ids plus `scheduler_name` | Use `check_job_status()` (`source = "scheduler"`). |
| Untracked, unsubmitted object | Error with a hint (`+ track()` / `submit()`). |
| Untracked but submitted object | Use `.submission` scheduler id via `check_job_status()` (`source = "scheduler"`). |

## 9.2 `refresh`

`status(x, refresh = FALSE)` is the default: one local DB read; read-only; works
offline. `refresh = TRUE` runs reconciliation with writes (Section 11) before
reading. When `refresh = FALSE`, print a **staleness hint** if there are
unapplied breadcrumbs or non-terminal rows, e.g.:

```
2 jobs RUNNING; last updated 17:31. Use status(refresh = TRUE) to check the scheduler.
```

## 9.3 Printing (`class_job_status`)

Use the existing `cli` style (themed rows via `cli::cli_format_method`, like
`.format_job_summary()` in `R/print_job.R`). Show the query time. For a
sequence, show an upstream-to-downstream tree. Show `note` when present.

```
<hpcR status> source: tracking (./.hpcR/hpcR_preproc.sqlite)  queried 17:44:10
 preproc   4821   COMPLETED   job   (recovered from breadcrumb: hpcR_not_found)
   +- model  4822   COMPLETED   job
   +- report 4823   SKIPPED     inferred   (upstream "model" FAILED)
```

# Compute side (templates, hooks, fallbacks)

## 10.1 Responsibilities

The scheduler templates own `RUNNING`, `COMPLETED` and `FAILED` for **all
languages**. Rationale: they see the real exit code and signals, work for non-R
jobs, and see failures before R starts. `run_r_job.R` does not write
`RUNNING/COMPLETED/FAILED` in phase 1 (this resolves its status `TODO`s):

| `run_r_job.R` TODO | Handled by |
|---|---|
| STARTED (before packages load) | template, just before `Rscript` |
| FAILED + cascade after the main `tryCatch` | template (non-zero exit via `stop()`) |
| FAILED after saving output / post-subs code (commented out) | template (non-zero exit) |
| COMPLETED (end of script) | template (exit 0) |
| add parents / `wait_for_job` on sub-jobs / sub-job failure | `run_r_job.R` (phase 2) |

Remove the empty `update_job_status()` stub from `run_r_job.R`.

## 10.2 `inst/` layout

```
inst/
  templates/  submit_to_slurm.sbatch  submit_to_torque.pbs  submit_to_local.sh
  runners/    run_r_job.R
  shell/      tracking_hooks.sh      # bash functions sourced by all three templates
  bin/        tracking_update.R      # CLI entry point (phase 2: tracking_add_child.R, tracking_tag.R)
```

Update `.get_system_file()` in `R/compile_job.R` to one lookup of
`templates/<file>` and `runners/<file>`. Tests only check `basename()`.
Pass the hooks and CLI paths to templates the same way `run_system_file` is
passed today.

## 10.3 Environment variables (set only for tracked jobs)

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `HPCR_TRACKING_DB` | DB path. **If unset, every hook is a no-op.** |
| `HPCR_TRACKING_TIMEOUT` | busy/hook timeout in seconds |
| `HPCR_TRACKING_CASCADE` | `TRUE`/`FALSE` |
| `HPCR_OBJECT_ID` | hpcR job object id |
| `HPCR_SEQUENCE_ID` | sequence id (if any) |
| `HPCR_LIB` | hpcR's library directory on the submitting machine |
| `HPCR_BREADCRUMB` | `<job_directory>/.hpcR/pending/<db basename>.log` |

The scheduler job id comes from the existing `JOB_ID` export in the templates.
Build the values in `.tracking_env_vars(job)` (in `R/submit_job.R`).

## 10.4 Hooks

`inst/shell/tracking_hooks.sh` defines:

* `hpcr_track_running`
* `hpcr_track_finish <exit_code>` (exit 0 -> `COMPLETED`; otherwise
  `FAILED` with `--cascade` when `HPCR_TRACKING_CASCADE` is `TRUE`)
* `hpcr_track_signal <SIG>` (used by traps for `SIGTERM SIGINT SIGHUP SIGQUIT`)

Template flow (the existing `set -euo pipefail` must not abort before
reporting):

```bash
source "$hpcr_hooks_file"
trap 'hpcr_track_signal TERM' TERM    # likewise INT HUP QUIT
hpcr_track_running

set +e
"${R_HOME}/bin/Rscript" --vanilla "$run_system_file" ...   # or the non-R command
job_status=$?
set -e

hpcr_track_finish "$job_status"
exit "$job_status"
```

Wall-time kills usually send `SIGTERM` first, so many timeouts are reported by
the **job** (`FAILED`, `reported_by = JOB`). Only `SIGKILL`, out-of-memory
kills and node failures reach reconciliation as scheduler-reported.

`inst/bin/tracking_update.R`: `--db --job_id --status --cascade --timeout`.
Parses flags (copy the small `parse_args` style used by `run_r_job.R`), prepends
`HPCR_LIB` to `.libPaths()`, loads hpcR, and calls the internal
`.cli_tracking_update()` in `R/tracking.R`. That function: builds the backend,
`tracking_resolve_id(retries = 40, wait = 0.25)` for the short-job race (the
`RUNNING` write can arrive before the row exists), then `tracking_update()`.

## 10.5 Failure handling: tracking can never hurt a job

Principle: a hook failure **never changes the job's exit code, never hangs it,
and always leaves a trace**. Do **not** add hpcR to the job's `packages()`
(`run_r_job.R`'s `load_packages()` aborts on a missing package, which would
fail the job over a tracking problem).

Layers, in order:

1. **Find hpcR.** Prepend `HPCR_LIB` to `.libPaths()`; use the same
   `${R_HOME}/bin/Rscript` the job uses.
2. **Guard the call.** Run the hook's `Rscript` under `timeout` (default 30 s)
   followed by `|| true`.
3. **Failure causes** handled by step 4: hpcR missing; DBI/RSQLite missing; DB
   path not visible from the node; DB locked past its timeout; DB schema newer
   than the installed hpcR (the script refuses to write).
4. **Breadcrumb.** The bash hook appends one tab-separated line to
   `$HPCR_BREADCRUMB` using plain `printf >>` (no R needed):
   `timestamp<TAB>job_id<TAB>status<TAB>exit_code<TAB>reason<TAB>host`.
   Small appends are effectively atomic on POSIX filesystems. If the directory
   is not writable, print the same line to the job's own log.
5. **One clear warning** to the job log per failure *kind*
   (`[hpcR tracking] could not write RUNNING: <reason>`), not per hook.
6. **Repair later.** `status(refresh = TRUE)` / `tracking_reconcile()` reads the
   breadcrumb file (Section 11.4), then asks the scheduler about the rest.
7. **Surface it.** The staleness hint (Section 9.2) and the row `note`.

Breadcrumb file facts: it is hpcR-specific (not a scheduler log), one file per
DB beside the job directory's `.hpcR/`, written **only** when a hook fails
(~100 bytes/line, 2-3 lines per job), so size is negligible (worst case 100k
jobs ~ 30 MB). No pruning in phase 1; document this. If needed later: rename the
file atomically, read and apply it, put unapplied lines back; prune fully
applied lines older than N days. Never rewrite in place (races appenders).
Applied lines stay as an audit trail; `tracking_events` records the applied
`event_key`s so reapplication is a no-op.

## 10.6 Worked fallback examples

**Example 1: hpcR missing on the node (Slurm job 4821).**
`hpcr_track_running` calls `Rscript`; `loadNamespace("hpcR")` fails. The hook
appends `2026-11-21T17:31:02 4821 RUNNING - hpcR_not_found` to the breadcrumb
file and prints one warning to the job log. The job runs and finishes;
`hpcr_track_finish 0` fails the same way and appends a `COMPLETED` line
(exit code 0, no repeated warning). The DB still says `QUEUED`. Later,
`status(job, refresh = TRUE)` reads both lines, applies `RUNNING` (17:31) and
`COMPLETED` (17:44) as job-reported with compare-and-set writes, records the
event keys, and prints
`COMPLETED (recovered from breadcrumb: hpcR_not_found)`. The breadcrumb is
better evidence than the scheduler here (it has the exit code and exact end
time, which `sacct`/`qstat`/`ps` may not).

**Example 2: killed before it can report (out of memory).** `RUNNING` was
written normally. The kernel sends `SIGKILL`; no hook runs, no breadcrumb.
`status(refresh = TRUE)` asks Slurm, sees `FAILED` (`OUT_OF_MEMORY`), sets
`FAILED` with `reported_by = SCHEDULER`, and the cascade marks downstream rows
`SKIPPED` (`reported_by = INFERRED`).

**Example 3: DB not visible from the node.** The DB is on a login-node-only
disk. The hook cannot open it and writes a breadcrumb under the job directory;
if that is also invisible it prints the line to the job log only. On the
submitting machine the DB says `QUEUED` while the scheduler says `COMPLETED`;
reconciliation fixes this for non-local jobs, and exact times can be recovered
from the log.

**Example 4: DB schema newer than the node's hpcR.** The hook sees
`user_version` is higher than it understands, refuses to write, and logs a
breadcrumb with reason `schema_newer` and a warning to update hpcR on the node.

**Example 5: local job.** Same machine, so hpcR is almost always present. If a
hook fails anyway, the breadcrumb is the only record. Reconciliation **never**
sets a local row to `COMPLETED` from absence in `ps`, but may from a breadcrumb
(the job itself reported success).

# Reconciliation

Implemented by `tracking_reconcile(backend, dry_run = TRUE, ...)`. `status(x,
refresh = TRUE)` calls it with `dry_run = FALSE`.

## 11.1 Reported by the job vs by the scheduler

* **Job-reported:** the job's own hook (or its breadcrumb) said so. Knows the
  true exit code and can report a `SIGTERM` before dying. Cannot report if killed
  with `SIGKILL`, if the node dies, or before the hook runs.
* **Scheduler-reported:** `sacct`/`qstat`/`ps` says so. Authoritative about
  whether the job is queued/running/ended and about out-of-memory and node
  failures; less precise about *why* something ended, and may forget the job
  (Torque after its keep time; `tracejob` needs server logs).

## 11.2 Which rows

Pending rows: status `QUEUED`, `RUNNING`, `SUSPENDED`, or `reported_by =
INFERRED` (e.g. `SKIPPED`). Group by `scheduler_name`; query in chunks of 200.
If the scheduler query returns `UNAVAILABLE`, stop early (do not write).

## 11.3 Action table

| DB row | Scheduler says | Action | Write |
|---|---|---|---|
| `QUEUED`/`RUNNING`/`SUSPENDED` | `FAILED` / `CANCELLED` | `UPDATE_TERMINAL` | set status, `reported_by = SCHEDULER`, end time if available; run cascade |
| `QUEUED`/`RUNNING` | `COMPLETED` (non-local only) | `UPDATE_TERMINAL` | set `COMPLETED`, `SCHEDULER` |
| `QUEUED` | `RUNNING` | `UPDATE_RUNNING` | set `RUNNING` |
| `RUNNING` | `QUEUED` (requeue) | `UNCHANGED` | none |
| `SKIPPED` (inferred) | `CANCELLED` / `FAILED` | `CONFIRM` | `reported_by = SCHEDULER` |
| `SKIPPED` (inferred) | `QUEUED` (still waiting) | `UNRESOLVED` | none; `note`: cancel it |
| `SKIPPED` (inferred) | job actually ran (`RUNNING`/`COMPLETED`/...) | `CORRECT` | set actual status; clear inferred flag |
| any pending | `MISSING` / `UNKNOWN` / `UNAVAILABLE` | `UNRESOLVED` | none |
| job-reported terminal | a **different** terminal | `CONFLICT` | **never overwrite**; report only |

Local rows are never set to `COMPLETED` from scheduler absence.
Writes use compare-and-set (`expected_status`) and happen only when
`dry_run = FALSE`. Use scheduler end times when present, else the current time.
"`SKIPPED` check": reconciliation also uses the edge's `afterok` signal for
more evidence (if the signal is `afterok`, an upstream failure confirms the
`SKIPPED` inference; if `afterany`, a `SKIPPED` row should not exist and is
flagged `CORRECT`).

## 11.4 Order of operations

1. Read breadcrumb files (distinct `job_tracking.breadcrumb` paths); apply
   unseen events (job-reported truth) using `tracking_events` for idempotency.
2. Select pending rows; query the scheduler; build the action table.
3. If `dry_run = FALSE`, apply actions, then run the cascade for newly terminal
   rows.
4. Return the action tibble (columns: `row_id`, `job_name`, `db_status`,
   `scheduler_status`, `action`, `applied`, `note`).

## 11.5 Scheduler differences

| | Slurm | Torque | Local |
|---|---|---|---|
| Source | `sacct -X -P` | `qstat -f`, then `tracejob` | `ps` |
| Failure of the query | non-zero exit -> `UNAVAILABLE` (changed from `MISSING`) | per-job calls; unreachable -> `UNAVAILABLE` | n/a |
| Forgets jobs? | after the accounting retention period | after the site's keep time; `tracejob` needs logs | immediately |
| Cancel detection | state `CANCELLED` | text regex (`cancel\|deleted\|removed\|qdel`) | none |
| `COMPLETED` from scheduler | trusted | trusted (exit status 0) | **not trusted** (absence means "gone", not "succeeded") |
| Dependency never satisfied | `PENDING` + `DependencyNeverSatisfied` | held | polling-based |

# Tags (phase 1)

`track(tags = list(subject = "01", step = "preproc"))` stores user-supplied
key/value info at submit time in `job_tags` with `source = "SUBMIT"`.
Values are coerced to character; keys must be non-empty, unique, and valid
names. `status()` can show tags (optionally as columns). In BrainGnomes the
analogous fields (`stage`, `sub_id`, etc.) were pipeline-defined and came from
a manifest, **not** user-supplied; hpcR tags are genuinely user-supplied.

# Phase 2 (design only, do not build now)

## 13.1 Sub-jobs spawned from inside a job

* `spawn(<job>)` (in `R/sugar.R`) called in a running script reads the parent
  identity from the `HPCR_*` environment variables, inherits the DB and
  `sequence_id`, registers the child row with `parent_row` set (unlimited depth,
  no levels). Outside a tracked job it falls back to plain `submit()` with a
  message.
* The user marks the parent with something like
  `sequencing(expect_children = TRUE)` so tracking knows to wait.
* Effective parent status: its own script `COMPLETED` only means its code ended.
  Effective status stays `RUNNING` until all children are terminal; a `FAILED`
  child makes the effective parent `FAILED`.
* `run_r_job.R` gets the "add parents" step and the `wait_for_job(SUB_JOB_IDS,
  ...)` step (the commented-out code), with the failure rule: if
  `all_subs_success` is violated, `stop()` (the template writes `FAILED`).
  `inst/bin/tracking_add_child.R` is the CLI version for non-R jobs.
* `tracking_cascade(include_children = )` is added. The failure cascade goes
  downstream but not back into the failing job's own children.
* **Open decision:** a downstream job's dependency is fixed at submit time,
  before children exist. Options: the parent waits via `wait_for_job()` on its
  children; a sentinel job (BrainGnomes has `postprocess_sentinel` scripts in
  `inst/hpc_scripts`); or edit the downstream dependency afterwards
  (`scontrol update ... Dependency=`, `qalter -W depend=`).

## 13.2 Inline runtime tags

`tag(n_rows = 1204)` writes to `job_tags` with `source = "RUNTIME"` (re-tagging
overwrites the value; `set_at` records when). Useful when the information is
only known during the job. Keep it small and scalar. Failures warn and never
abort the job; outside a tracked job it is a no-op with a message.
`inst/bin/tracking_tag.R` is the CLI version. Phase 2 reuses the same `HPCR_*`
environment plumbing and the same hook-failure principles (Section 10.5).

# Tests

* **Status vocabulary:** `.standardize_statuses()` returns uppercase; update
  `test-status-wait.R`, `test-run.R`, `test-submit-invoke.R`.
* **submit/job_id:** return value carries `.submission`; `job_id()` for job,
  sequence, unsubmitted; print method shows the id; guard hint.
* **track():** default DB path; explicit path; sequence `+` applies to all
  members; overwrite warning names jobs; conflicting explicit DBs error;
  partial-tracking message and warning.
* **Backend:** schema creation/versioning; register/update/query round-trip;
  compare-and-set; resolve-id retry; refusing to write a newer schema.
* **Cascade:** by `signal` (`afterok`, `aftercorr`, `afternotok`, `afterany`);
  `SKIPPED` + `INFERRED`; already-terminal rows untouched.
* **status():** each resolution path; `refresh = FALSE` is read-only; staleness
  hint; print snapshot; `as.data.frame`.
* **Hooks/fallback (simulated failures):** hpcR missing (empty `R_LIBS`), DBI
  missing, read-only DB, locked DB, newer schema, hung hook (timeout). In every
  case: job exit code unchanged, breadcrumb written, reconciliation applies it
  and is idempotent.
* **Reconciliation:** every row of the action table with mocked scheduler
  output; local never `COMPLETED` from absence; `CONFLICT` never overwrites.
* **Template tests:** use the existing local-scheduler test setup (see
  `test-run.R`) where possible; skip scheduler-specific tests when `sbatch`/
  `qsub` are absent, as the current tests do.

   compile/submit tests pass unchanged.
2. **Uppercase statuses** everywhere + tests. *Check:* no lowercase status
   literals remain (grep); suite passes.
3. **`.submission`, `job_id()`, `submit()` return, print, guard hint.**
4. **Classes, generics, SQLite backend** (`R/tracking.R`, `job_classes.R`).
5. **`track()`, DB resolution, sequence `+`, tags, edges/signals.**
6. **Submit-time registration, env vars, hooks, `tracking_update.R`,
   fallbacks/breadcrumbs.** *Check:* simulated-failure tests pass.
7. **`status()`, `class_job_status`, reconciliation.**
8. **Tests, docs, vignette, NEWS.** *Check:* `devtools::check()` clean of new
   warnings.

# Appendix A: BrainGnomes to hpcR mapping

| BrainGnomes | hpcR |
|---|---|
| `STARTED` | `RUNNING` |
| `FAILED_BY_EXT` | `SKIPPED` (`reported_by = INFERRED`) |
| `parent_id` + `child_level` | `job_dependencies` edge table (+ reserved `parent_row`) |
| `job_obj` BLOB per row | not carried over |
| `job_contracts`, manifests, receipts | deferred |
| `capture_output_manifest()` | deferred |
| `inst/upd_job_status.R` | `inst/bin/tracking_update.R` + `inst/shell/tracking_hooks.sh` |
| `inst/insert_tracked_job.R` | not needed (registration happens in R inside `submit()`) |
| `inst/add_parent.R` | phase 2 `inst/bin/tracking_add_child.R` (no level) |
| `reconcile_tracked_jobs()` | `tracking_reconcile()` |
| 40-column wide table + `ALTER TABLE` migrations | narrow table + `user_version` |

# Appendix B: audit checklist (quick yes/no review)

* [ ] Tracking is opt-in; nothing changes for users who never call `track()`.
* [ ] One uppercase vocabulary everywhere; `SKIPPED` replaces `FAILED_BY_EXT`.
* [ ] upstream/downstream used for sequences; parent/child only for sub-jobs.
* [ ] `submit()` returns the object; `job_id()` works; print shows the id.
* [ ] All jobs in a sequence share one DB; conflicting explicit paths error.
* [ ] Edges store `signal`; cascade follows the signal table.
* [ ] Hooks are no-ops without `HPCR_TRACKING_DB`; hook failure never alters
      exit code or hangs; breadcrumb always written on failure.
* [ ] `status()` default is read-only and offline-safe; staleness hint shown.
* [ ] Reconciliation never overwrites a job-reported conflict; never marks local
      `COMPLETED` from absence; idempotent.
* [ ] Only one new R file (`R/tracking.R`); `inst/` is in subfolders.
